messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: P1 - GPU queue growth detected in us-west1 primary pool. avg queue depth 122s, tail latency 2.3s, autoscaler errors observed (ProvisionTimeout, QuotaExceeded). Paging oncall: Tess (oncall-sre). https://grafana.redwood/in/r/queue-overview
Tess (oncall-sre): Ack. I'm pulling metrics now. tagging Luis and Priya.
Tess (oncall-sre): First check: is this a transient burst or autoscaler stuck?
Priya (runtime): seeing repeated errors from cloud provider: "InstanceProvisionFailure: InsufficientAcceleratorCapacity" in us-west1 zones. Autoscaler retries hit backoff.
Luis (infra): Confirmed. Also see API quota error 429 when trying to attach GPUs to new nodes: rate limit from cloud project.
Ben (support): We're getting several customer reports of throttled requests and 500s, mostly from customers pinned to us-west1. Severity is high for three paying accounts.
Tess (oncall-sre): Impact: degraded for hosted API customers with region affinity to us-west1. Not global outage yet. Prioritize mitigation to keep P95 latency under SLO.
Tess (oncall-sre): Quick mitigations I propose: 1) Flip routing to allow spillover to us-central1/eu-west1 for non-pinned requests, 2) Lower concurrency quotas for low-tier keys to shed load, 3) Temporarily enable fallback to smaller model-variants for best-effort tiers. Thoughts?
Priya (runtime): I can update routing policy in Router service to lower the primary-region preference and increase spillover ratio within 2-3m. Will prepare a manual override.
Luis (infra): I can also open emergency capacity request with cloud support, but ETA 30-90m. Meanwhile, we should avoid autoscaler thrash. Recommend turning off aggressive scale-down and increase max nodes if we can until provisioning stabilizes.
Clara (product): Heads up: I'll prepare a short status note for affected customers. Which customers are impacted most? Ben, can you list top 5?
Ben (support): Top 5 are: acme-inc, noteboards, fastdocs, convoai (Enterprise), and studyhub. acme-inc & convoai are on dedicated capacity pinned to us-west1 which complicates reroute.
Tess (oncall-sre): Note: dedicated pools pinned to us-west1 cannot be rerouted automatically. For hosted customers we can spillover. We need to reduce queue by shedding lower-priority work.
Priya (runtime): Executing routing override: PATCH /routing/overrides {"region_preference":{"us-west1":0.6,"us-central1":0.2,"eu-west1":0.2}} 
Priya (runtime): applying now...
incident-bot: action: routing-override applied by Priya. override_id=rv-20260315-1
Tess (oncall-sre): Enabling fallback model variants for best-effort keys: runtime-config set fallback_model=llama-mini for tier=free,trial.
Priya (runtime): done. This should reduce per-request GPU time for non-paying traffic.
Luis (infra): Increasing max_nodes for us-west1 pool from 40 -> 60 to reduce autoscaler restarts (manual override). Executing cluster resize...
Luis (infra): resize command output:
```
gcloud compute --project redwood resize-instance-group us-west1-gpu-pool --size=60
Operation started: operation-12345
Status: RUNNING -> DONE
```
Tess (oncall-sre): Good. Also temporarily disabled autoscaler aggressive scale-in to avoid churn: set scale_down_disabled=true for 20m.
Priya (runtime): Routing metrics show spillover traffic ramping to us-central1 now. Queue depth in us-west1 starting to drop from 122s -> 48s. P95 latency trending down slowly.
Ben (support): Customer update drafted: "We're seeing increased latency in us-west1 due to GPU provisioning issues. We're routing traffic to alternate regions and enabling mitigations — we'll provide updates every 30m." Clara to review.
Clara (product): Reviewed, sending now.
Tess (oncall-sre): Note dedicated customers acme-inc & convoai: we need to coordinate migrations or manual failovers. Luis — can we provision temporary dedicated nodes in us-central1 and attach their workloads?
Luis (infra): We can provision a temporary dedicated pool in us-central1 but for dedicated licenses we need approval from sales/legal. For immediate relief, we can offer a stop-gap: create a reserved node group and route only non-sensitive workloads. This requires config changes from Priya.
Priya (runtime): I can create a routed pool and tag it for enterprise-approval=false so it picks up only non-pinned traffic. Creating pool now...
Priya (runtime): new pool us-central1-temp-dedicated created, capacity 8 gpus.
incident-bot: Note: manual pool creation logged (pool_id=us-central1-temp-dedicated).
Tess (oncall-sre): Good. For dedicated pinned accounts that need immediate SLA, we will coordinate postmortem for longer-term solutions. For now, support to inform them about mitigation window.
Ben (support): Reached out to convoai & acme-inc, both acknowledged and asked for ETA. Gave provisional ETA 60-120m.
Priya (runtime): Alert: one of the container image pulls failing in us-west1 during node spin-up due to registry throttling. Switching to fallback image host.
Luis (infra): Registry throttle workaround applied. New nodes are now healthy and joining the pool.
Tess (oncall-sre): Monitoring: us-west1 queue depth now 22s, p95 latency 1.1s. Continued spillover to us-central1 at ~30% of traffic.
Clara (product): Any customer-visible errors continuing?
Ben (support): A handful of 500 spikes for some long-running requests, but trending down. No new Sev1 customer report after the routing change.
Tess (oncall-sre): Next steps: 1) Keep routing override in place until pool health stable 2) Start root-cause: why cloud reported InsufficientAcceleratorCapacity and quota 429s 3) Postmortem template & action items (increase cross-region capacity, improve autoscaler backoff, add early spillover if provisioning errors) 4) Follow-up with customers.
Priya (runtime): I'm collecting logs for autoscaler and router, will upload to the incident doc. Also will add a metric alert: if ProvisionFailureRate > 5% for 5m then auto-trigger earlier cross-region spillover.
Luis (infra): I'll file a support ticket with cloud (Ticket #CLOUD-7890) and request capacity reservation for next 24h.
Tess (oncall-sre): Thanks all. Removing paging alert as mitigations are in place. Reopen if metrics regress.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: P1 mitigated to P2. Queue depth decreased below alert threshold. Full incident doc: https://confluence.redwood.io/incidents/2018003456
Clara (product): Good work. Let's reconvene in 2h for postmortem.
Ben (support): Will follow up with customers and close support tickets once they confirm stability.
Tess (oncall-sre): End of thread summary: Cause - GPU capacity shortage + registry/quotas causing autoscaler failures. Mitigations - routing override to spillover regions, fallback model for low-tier traffic, manual pool resize, registry fallback, temporarily disabled aggressive scale-down. Action items assigned in incident doc.
